                                          Affidavit of Michael P. Gorman

       Michael P. Gorman, being first duly swom, on her oath states:

        l.       My name is Michael P. Gorman. I am a Managing Principal with Brubaker &
Associates, Inc., having its principal place of business at 16690 Swingley Ridge Road, Suite 140,
Chesterfield, Missouri 63017. We have been retained by Federal Executive Agencies (*FEA"),
and Louisiana Energy Services, L.L.C. d/b/a URENCO USA in this proceeding on their behalf.

       2.       Attached hereto and made a part hereof for all purposes is my settlement testimony
in support of the Contested Comprehensive Stipulation which was prepared in written form for
irrtroduction into evidence in Case No. 25-00079-UT.

       3.        I hereby swear and affirm that the testimony         true                   shows

           Settlement Testimony of Michael P. Gorman in Support of the Stipulation
                             NMPRC Case No. 25-00079-UT


 1   Q       PLEASE STATE YOUR NAME AND BUSINESS ADDRESS.

 2   A       Michael P. Gorman. My business address is 16690 Swingley Ridge Road,

 3           Suite 140, Chesterfield, MO 63017.



 4   Q       ARE      YOU      THE      SAME       MICHAEL         P.    GORMAN         WHO

 5           PREVIOUSLY FILED TESTIMONY IN THIS CASE?

 6   A       Yes, on May 1, 2026, I filed direct testimony on behalf of Federal Executive

 7           Agencies (“FEA”), and Louisiana Energy Services, L.L.C. (“LES”) d/b/a

 8           URENCO USA.



 9   Q       WHAT IS THE PURPOSE OF YOUR SETTLEMENT TESTIMONY

10           IN THIS PROCEEDING?

11   A       My testimony supports the contested agreement and stipulation between

12           Southwestern Public Service Company (“SPS” or “Company”) and other

13           parties in this case. As outlined in the Contested Comprehensive Stipulation

14           (“Stipulation”),1 SPS and other parties to this case resolved the major




             1
              The term “Comprehensive Stipulation” refers the Comprehensive Stipulation that
     was filed in this docket on June 22, 2026. The term “Signatories” is defined on page 2 of
     the Stipulation to include all parties who are joining the Stipulation. As explained in the
     Stipulation, the Staff does not oppose parts of the stipulation, and the New Mexico Energy
     Minerals and Natural Resources Department has not taken a position on the Stipulation.

                                              Page 1
          Settlement Testimony of Michael P. Gorman in Support of the Stipulation
                            NMPRC Case No. 25-00079-UT


 1         differences for establishing a revenue requirement, spread of the revenue

 2         requirements across rate classes, and rate design for this case.

 3                In my testimony, I will comment on and explain why I support these

 4         key elements of the Stipulation in this proceeding.



 5   Q     PLEASE SUMMARIZE THE STIPULATION FINDING ON THE

 6         APPROPRIATE REVENUE REQUIREMENT.

 7   A     SPS’s initial application sought an increase in revenue requirement of

 8         $175.3 million. The Stipulation adjusted this revenue requirement increase

 9         down to $90.0 million. This revenue increase aligned with many of the

10         overall findings and recommendations made by the various parties in this

11         proceeding.    I believe the agreed upon adjustments to the revenue

12         requirement reasonably resolve the findings on SPS’ retail cost of service

13         and will provide SPS a fair and reasonable opportunity to earn a fair overall

14         rate of return on the infrastructure used to provide service in New Mexico.

15         The settlement also reasonably resolves the appropriation of the settlement

16         revenue requirement across rate classes, the adjustment to rate class rates to

17         allow SPS to recover its cost of service from each rate class, and

18         adjustments to various tariff rate and rider mechanisms to result in just and




                                          Page 2
           Settlement Testimony of Michael P. Gorman in Support of the Stipulation
                             NMPRC Case No. 25-00079-UT


 1          reasonable charges to customers based on economic and efficient utility

 2          management and at rates that are just and reasonable.



 3   Q      DOES       THE     STIPULATION            CONTAIN       A    REASONABLE

 4          OVERALL RATE OF RETURN?

 5   A      Yes.    The Stipulation’s ratemaking capital structure is reasonable in

 6          combination with a stipulated Return On Equity (“ROE”) of 9.5%. The

 7          stipulated overall rate of return was the result of meaningful negotiations

 8          between the parties. Notably, the stipulated ROE of 9.5% was well within

 9          the multiple ROE recommendations offered by various parties in this case,

10          including FEA and LES.2 I believe the resulting overall rate of return of

11          7.59%, along with modifications to the Company’s proposed depreciation

12          rate will support SPS’s credit metrics and its investment grade bond rating,

13          and will do so at reasonable tariff rates to New Mexico customers.




            2
             See, e.g., Direct Testimony of Christopher C. Walters (“Walters Dir.”) for LES-
     FEA at 2;

                                             Page 3
          Settlement Testimony of Michael P. Gorman in Support of the Stipulation
                            NMPRC Case No. 25-00079-UT


 1   Q     DOES THE STIPULATION REFLECT A COMPROMISE ON

 2         DEPRECIATION RATES?

 3   A     Yes. Section 1.2 of the Stipulation provides for adjustments to depreciation

 4         rates but does not increase the revenue requirement in this case. The

 5         Stipulation accomplished this revenue neutral result in part by extending the

 6         lives of various generating resources as outlined in Section 1.2 to the

 7         stipulation.



 8   Q     ARE     THE     STIPULATION          DEPRECIATION           RATES      AND

 9         AGREEMENTS ON SERVICE LIFE-EXTENSION FOR SEVERAL

10         GENERATING RESOURCES FAIR AND REASONABLE?

11   A     Yes. Many parties viewed the extension of the service lives of Jones Units

12         1 and 2, Nichols Units 1-3, Maddox Units 1 and 2, Plant X Unit 4, and Tolk

13         Units 1 and 2 as reasonable. Extending the life of these units provides SPS

14         needed generating capacity to meet its SPP resource adequacy obligation

15         and lowers SPS’s New Mexico annual revenue requirement.




                                          Page 4
          Settlement Testimony of Michael P. Gorman in Support of the Stipulation
                            NMPRC Case No. 25-00079-UT


 1   Q     DOES THE STIPULATION INCLUDE A PROVISION FOR THE

 2         JURISDICTIONAL ALLOCATION OF THE CUNNINGHAM

 3         BATTERY ENERGY STORAGE SYSTEM (“BESS”)?

 4   Y     Yes. The Stipulation reflects that the Cunningham BESS is primarily

 5         needed to meet New Mexico’s environmental objectives but also provides

 6         New Mexico with accredited capacity benefits. Hence, in developing a

 7         jurisdictional production capacity allocation, Cunningham BESS will be

 8         directly assigned to New Mexico and the additional capacity needed to meet

 9         New Mexico’s resource capacity will be allocated from the SPS system

10         portfolio using the jurisdictional production capacity allocator. However,

11         the New Mexico coincident peaks will be reduced by the Cunningham

12         accredited capacity that is directly assigned to New Mexico. This

13         methodology ensures that New Mexico is not allocated system resource

14         capacity costs that are in excess of the system capacity needed to provide

15         reliable service in New Mexico.




                                         Page 5
          Settlement Testimony of Michael P. Gorman in Support of the Stipulation
                            NMPRC Case No. 25-00079-UT


 1   Q     DOES THE STIPULATION CONTAIN A PROVISION FOR THE

 2         AMORTIZATION PERIOD FOR PREVIOUSLY APPROVED

 3         REGULATORY ASSETS AND DEBITS?

 4   A     Yes. The Stipulation develops a proposed amortization period for Excess

 5         Liability Insurance (“ELI”) premiums, legacy meter costs, and community

 6         solar program costs. See Section 1.7 of the Stipulation.

 7                The Stipulation also provides that SPS may earn a return on the

 8         Deferred Tax Asset (“DTA”) costs at the cost of long-term debt for the

 9         PTCs created at Plant X and Cunningham Solar to the extent the PTCs are

10         unused or are not transferred.

11                The Stipulation outlines the treatment for Investment Tax Credits

12         (“ITC”) for Cunningham BESS and Plant X BESS, and specifies

13         amortization over a five-year period, which provides that the unamortized

14         balance will earn the stipulated Weighted Average Cost of Capital

15         (“WACC”). The Cunningham BESS amortization will begin with the

16         effective date of the rates approved in this case, and the Plant X BESS

17         amortization will begin upon its commercial operation date.

18                Further, the Stipulation allows SPS to recover transfer costs capped

19         at 10% of the nominal value for PTCs at Hale and Sagamore Wind projects




                                            Page 6
          Settlement Testimony of Michael P. Gorman in Support of the Stipulation
                            NMPRC Case No. 25-00079-UT


 1         through SPS’s Fuel Purchased Power Cost Adjustment Clause

 2         (“FPPCAC”).

 3                These stipulated treatments of tax benefits and tax deferrals are fair

 4         and reasonable.



 5   Q     DOES THE STIPULATION DEVELOP THE RATEMAKING

 6         TREATMENT FOR ALL SYSTEM SALES MARGINS OF

 7         CUNNINGHAM AND PLANT X SOLAR PROJECTS?

 8   A     Yes. The Stipulation in Section 1.9 says SPS will not retain any system

 9         sales margin for these resources after the resource cost recovery commences

10         from New Mexico retail customers. The treatment of market sales margins

11         before cost recovery begins is fair and reasonable.



12   Q     DOES THE STIPULATION RESOLVE ISSUES RELATED TO

13         REVENUE ALLOCATION AND RATE DESIGN?

14   A     Yes. The Stipulation found that it is appropriate to include Sagamore and

15         Hale Wind Generation as components of SPS’s generation resource

16         portfolio and allocate the portfolio within the retail class cost of service

17         using an Average and Excess Four Coincident Peak (“A&E 4CP”)




                                          Page 7
          Settlement Testimony of Michael P. Gorman in Support of the Stipulation
                            NMPRC Case No. 25-00079-UT


 1         methodology that has been used in past rate cases to allocate SPS resource

 2         portfolio costs.

 3                 The Stipulation further states that in developing the AED 4CP

 4         allocator, a study will be performed to determine how behind the meter

 5         generation will be reflected in the accurate measurement of production and

 6         transmission demand costs.



 7   Q     DOES THE STIPULATION ADDRESS THE LARGE GENERAL

 8         SERVICE TRANSMISSION (“LGS-T”) RATE DESIGN?

 9   A     Yes. The Stipulation agrees to the following:

10                 •   The demand rachet provision will be changed from a 60%
11                     demand ratchet to a 70% demand ratchet.

12                 •   Power factor credits for customers in the LGS class will
13                     continue.

14                 •    In designing the Renewable*Connect tariff, the parties agree
15                     that any administration costs that are already recovered in base
16                     rates will not also be recovered in Renewable*Connect rider
17                     charges.

18                 •   The Renewable*Connect production credit will be equivalent to
19                     the demand charge less the unbundled transmission demand
20                     charges included in the LGS-T tariff.

21                 •    It is appropriate to accept SPS’s proposed Time-Of-Use
22                     (“TOU”) fuel pilot.

23                 These tariff rates and rider provisions are fair and reasonable.


                                          Page 8
          Settlement Testimony of Michael P. Gorman in Support of the Stipulation
                            NMPRC Case No. 25-00079-UT


 1   Q     DOES THE STIPULATION MAKE ANY FINDINGS WITH

 2         RESPECT TO SLCA CREDITS IN RATE NO. 27?

 3   A     Yes. The Stipulation affirms that the production capacity cost credit in Rate

 4         No 27 would be set equal to the LGS-T 115kV production capacity cost

 5         recovered in the LGS-T 115 kV demand and energy charges. This provision

 6         is reasonable because it provides Cannon Air Force Base credit for the

 7         hydro-capacity the Western Area Power Administration (“WAPA”) has

 8         delivered to SPS, which is then used by SPS to provide service to its retail

 9         system. The government cost to deliver this hydro capacity is recovered in

10         the Rate No 27 production capacity cost credits. Updating the credits to the

11         production capacity cost included in LGS-T 115kV rate is fair and

12         reasonable.



13   Q     DID THE STIPULATION INCLUDE A PROVISION RELATED TO

14         DATA CENTERS AND LARGE LOAD TARIFFS?

15   A     Yes. The Stipulation describes that SPS will develop and file with the

16         Commission a new large load customer class tariff within six months of the

17         Commission approving the Stipulation, and the tariff will be designed in a

18         manner that ensures that large load customers are assigned SPS’s cost to

19         provide service, and will not shift costs or risks to other customer classes.


                                          Page 9
         Settlement Testimony of Michael P. Gorman in Support of the Stipulation
                           NMPRC Case No. 25-00079-UT




1   Q     DOES THIS COMPLETE YOUR TESTIMONY?

2   A     Yes, it does.
